# Workspace has no stated façade contract, so every extraction has to guess which callbacks the host still owes its collaborators

Sub of #18304 (Workspace decomposition). **The closer** — blocked by #18305, #18306, #18307, #18311 and #18317: a façade contract can only be written once the owners it fronts exist.

## The Problem

D#18150's Option G makes `Workspace` a façade — *cross-concern ordering and the one mutation boundary* — but no artifact states what that façade actually is. Each extraction currently has to infer which callbacks the host still owes, and an inferred contract is how a "façade" becomes a forwarding shell one method at a time.

There is a hard direction rule that must be written down because it is easy to violate in one import. @neo-fable stated it as two-way: **`manager.Transaction` never imports dock `Workspace` or `Document`** — *and* **`Workspace` never imports the manager either.** The second half has a measured cost behind it: `Workspace.mjs`'s static closure is **69 modules / 1,354 KB** and lands in every single-window app. A single upward import puts the whole topology manager into a single-window download.

## The Fix

State the seam explicitly as **`read` / `prepare` / `adopt` / `project` callbacks registered at bind time, in both directions** — no static import either way. Fold `WorkspaceSet` into the participant side (#18317 does the lifecycle half; this leaf closes the contract).

Then apply the no-regrowth ratchet (#18278) to the resulting façade, and record the final Ownership-test verdict for the file as a whole rather than per-cut.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Workspace` façade | D#18150 Option G | ordering + the one mutation boundary; `read`/`prepare`/`adopt`/`project` registered at bind | — | class docblock | the contract is the deliverable |
| import direction | @neo-fable, both-ways rule | no static import in either direction | — | docblock + guard | 69 modules / 1,354 KB closure |
| `window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` | D#18150 step 5 | folded; no duplicate registry | — | — | #18317 lands the lifecycle half |
| file size | #18278 ratchet | façade may only shrink from its post-extraction baseline | — | — | ratchet is the fence |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The façade contract is stated in `Workspace`'s class docblock as the four registered callbacks, with the ordering guarantees it provides.
- [ ] **Import-direction falsifier, mechanical:** a static-closure measurement shows `Workspace.mjs` imports no topology-manager module, and the manager imports no dock `Workspace`/`Document` module. Red-first against a deliberately added import in either direction.
- [ ] The single-window static closure does not grow: module count and KB recorded before and after, against the 69 / 1,354 KB baseline.
- [ ] `WorkspaceSet` is folded; no duplicate participant registry exists.
- [ ] **Final Ownership-test verdict** for `Workspace.mjs` as a whole: all four questions, with method count, config/state count, code lines and total lines at the closing head against the `131c782ca8` baseline (110 methods, 50 declarations, 1,742 code lines, 4,255 total).
- [ ] The #18278 ratchet is applied to the façade with its post-extraction baseline, which may only shrink.
- [ ] No proxy wrapper is retained for a retired subclass API — every surviving seam names a current product reason, per the operator's zero-backcompat ruling.

## Out of Scope

- Any individual extraction — they are the sibling leaves; this one only closes the contract over them.
- The band. If the architecture is right and the number is 2,100, the number moves; **hitting 1,500–2,000 is explicitly not a criterion.**

## Avoided Traps

- **Writing the façade contract first.** It would be a guess, and every extraction would then be measured against a guess.
- **A one-way import rule.** Stating only "the manager must not import the dock" leaves the expensive direction unguarded — the one that puts 1,354 KB into single-window apps.
- **Treating the LOC band as the finish line.** Two metrics are in play (#18304); the ratchet and the Ownership test are the gate, and the band can be met once and regrow.
- **An intermediate "dock controller"** to hold the leftovers. Named and rejected in the Step-Back: it keeps today's ownership under a new noun.
